Update a commitment ledger using the NEW CHUNK and EXISTING RECORDS.
Distinguish suggestions, intentions, firm commitments, conditional commitments, and uncertainty.
Requests/authorization/approval are not personal acceptance. A satisfied condition is not completion.
Keep tentative dates tentative. Reassignment requires acceptance; a request alone does not transfer ownership.
Retain cancelled, superseded, and completed obligations. Use the same id for revisions of the same task.
Record reported role/institutional responsibilities as such in uncertainty; do not invent personal acceptance.
Include relevant brief procedural undertakings as well as substantive tasks. Exclude general facts without tasks.

"conditions":"condition text or null", "deadline":"time text or null",
"status":"suggested|intended|conditional|active|condition_failed|completed|cancelled|uncertain",

Use actual JSON null when unknown. Every upsert needs exact quotes from the conversation seen so far,
including at least one quote in the NEW CHUNK. An empty upserts array is allowed.
Only output records that are new or changed. Keep quotations short. Do not omit qualifications to save space.

NEW CHUNK:
 Thank you, President Burgess. Thank you, Councilmember Harrell, for bringing this forward in your committee. As has been stated, this legislation, if but when passed, it will be very important anecdotally. Unfortunately, we don't have huge statistics, but anecdotally the message is very, very clear. Wage theft is rampant in Seattle. My office gets contacted by constituents regularly. That report wage theft or other violations of their law, of the labor law, of their rights. The companies that commit this crime continue to get away with it because if they're caught, they face little more consequence right now than having to pay the wages they should have paid in the first place. And as Gordon Brown mentioned in last year's budget council passed a statement of legislative intended. My office drafted asking the mayor's office to provide an ordinance increasing the penalties and remedies for wage theft. And I think that this legislation will successfully do that. Workers become eligible for three times what is stolen from them. Which will help them, those workers who may have built up debts after being underpaid their wages. And it will help also as a deterrent for unscrupulous business who may have maybe repeat offenders. There will eventually be a private rate of action so workers are empowered to pursue remedies for wage theft if the Office of Labor Standards is not able to. And as Councilmember Legarda correctly said, many workers, a whole host of workers in Seattle will be impacted by this law. But do make effective use of this improved law. Workers will still need to keep getting organized and educate each other of their rights. And moreover, we need more workers organized into unions. So in as a matter of fact, the effectiveness of a law like this of a legislation like this is enhanced by increased unionization, like the bill that we just passed for our bass drivers. I wanted to thank the labor movement for participating in the task force that reviewed the various proposals and fighting to make sure that it had meaningful, meaningful remedies and penalties.
